criterion: which fine-grained arxiv subject category (e.g. cs.LG, math.AG, hep-th) the paper title belongs to

categories.name: astro-ph
categories.definition: Papers concerning astrophysics, cosmology, stellar and planetary science, and astronomical observations.

categories.name: cond-mat
categories.definition: Papers on condensed matter physics, including materials science, quantum matter, and statistical mechanics of solids.

categories.name: gr-qc
categories.definition: Papers on general relativity, quantum cosmology, and gravitational physics.

categories.name: hep-ex
categories.definition: Papers on high-energy physics experiments, particle detectors, and accelerator physics.

categories.name: hep-th
categories.definition: Papers on high-energy physics theory, including quantum field theory and string theory.

categories.name: math
categories.definition: Papers on pure and applied mathematics, including algebra, geometry, analysis, and topology.

categories.name: nlin
categories.definition: Papers on nonlinear sciences, including chaotic dynamics, pattern formation, and cellular automata.

categories.name: physics
categories.definition: Papers on general physics, including fluid dynamics, optics, plasma physics, and geophysics.

categories.name: quant-ph
categories.definition: Papers on quantum physics, quantum information, and quantum computation.

categories.name: cs
categories.definition: Papers on computer science, including machine learning, software engineering, systems, and theory.

categories.name: math-ph
categories.definition: Papers on mathematical physics, focusing on the mathematical methods used in physics.

categories.name: q-bio

categories.name: q-fin

categories.name: stat

categories.name: eess

categories.name: econ
